description.value: A boat-in marine campsite on De Courcy Island in the Gulf Islands, set in a sheltered cove steeped in the lore of the infamous Brother Twelve; cyclists must arrange water transport as there is no road access whatsoever.

raw_osm.description: Walk-in sites with wooden tent pads, picnic tables, 1 vault, 1 composting toilets. Access from beach top via stair up steep bank to N. No fires permitted. Campers must remove all garbage.
raw_osm.description:landing: Easy on moderate to steep gradient shell, gravel beach facing Ruxton Passage in cove S of Pirates Cove proper. Some exposure to S.
raw_osm.description:other: Potable water at pump 200 m from tent area. Walking trails. 2 dinghy docks in main cove to NW. Anchorage in adjacent NW (main) cove.
raw_osm.name: Pirates Cove Campsite (BCMT)
raw_osm.reservation:description: Camping fees apply year-round. May pre-pay permit via Internet, but no reservable sites. Fee $5.00 per person per night (2019) via BC Parks Backcountry Registration System or in drop box near water pump.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: Primary evidence comes from OSM tags, which are detailed and specific: the description tag confirms walk-in tent pads, picnic tables, vault and composting toilets; description:other confirms potable water at a pump 200 m away; reservation:description explicitly states 'no reservable sites.' The fetched website content is almost entirely BC Parks navigation boilerplate with no Pirates Cove-specific text extracted, so OSM tags are the authoritative source for all amenity claims. The site is a BC Marine Trails campsite in a Provincial Marine Park, publicly accessible year-round per the reservation description.
concerns: Website content fetched is almost entirely BC Parks global navigation boilerplate — no Pirates Cove-specific page text was extracted, so all amenity detail relies solely on OSM tags.
Fee information in OSM reservation:description (CAD $5.00/person/night) is dated 2019 and likely outdated.
Site is primarily marine-access (BC Marine Trails); land-based cycling access to De Courcy Island requires ferry travel, which should be noted for directory users.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: A real, publicly accessible BC Provincial Marine Park campsite with confirmed facilities; open year-round per OSM data. Useful to touring cyclists travelling the Gulf Islands.
enrichment_extras.notes: Capacity: 6 tent sites. Additional OSM detail: walking trails on-site; 2 dinghy docks in main cove to NW; anchorage available in adjacent NW cove. Permit pre-payment available via BC Parks Backcountry Registration System (camping.bcparks.ca) or drop box near water pump.

wow_evidence: boat-in marine campsite... no road access whatsoever
